questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes the products of mitosis?
options: Two genetically identical nuclei with the same chromosome number as the parent
Two haploid nuclei that differ genetically
questions.answer: Two genetically identical nuclei with the same chromosome number as the parent
questions.hint: Mitosis is used for growth and repair.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes the typical products of meiosis?
options: Two haploid cells identical to the parent
questions.hint: Meiosis involves two divisions.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which stage of mitosis do chromosomes condense and the nuclear membrane break down?
questions.hint: It is the first stage.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a micrograph, chromosomes are lined up across the equator of the cell. Which stage is shown?
questions.hint: Spindle fibres are attached to the centromeres.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.hint: The chromatids look V-shaped as they are pulled.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a micrograph, two groups of chromosomes are at opposite poles and nuclear membranes are re-forming. Which stage is shown?
questions.hint: It is the last stage of mitosis.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: How does cytokinesis differ in plant cells compared with animal cells?
options: A cell plate forms between the two nuclei
A cleavage furrow pinches the cell in two
The nuclear membrane does not re-form
No new cell wall is made
questions.answer: A cell plate forms between the two nuclei
questions.hint: Plant cells have a rigid wall.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a root tip sample, 30 cells are in mitosis out of 240 cells counted. Calculate the mitotic index as a decimal.
questions.hint: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the process in prophase I in which non-sister chromatids exchange segments of DNA.
questions.hint: It happens at chiasmata.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which stage of meiosis does random orientation of bivalents occur?
questions.hint: Homologous pairs line up together in this stage.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An organism has a haploid number (n) of 3. How many different combinations of chromosomes are possible in its gametes due to random orientation alone?
questions.hint: Use 2ⁿ.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What can non-disjunction during meiosis cause?
options: Gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes
Gametes that are genetically identical to the parent
questions.answer: Gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes
questions.hint: Chromosomes fail to separate correctly.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the role of cyclins in the cell cycle?
options: They bind to and activate cyclin-dependent kinases, controlling progression through the cycle
They copy DNA during S phase
questions.answer: They bind to and activate cyclin-dependent kinases, controlling progression through the cycle
questions.hint: Their concentration rises and falls during the cycle.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is an oncogene?
options: A gene that, when mutated, can contribute to the development of cancer
A gene that only acts during meiosis
A protein that stops crossing over
A gene found only in plant cells
questions.answer: A gene that, when mutated, can contribute to the development of cancer
questions.hint: Think about uncontrolled cell division.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Compare and contrast mitosis and meiosis.
questions.hint: Include number of divisions, chromosome number of products, genetic variation and function.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain how meiosis generates genetic variation among gametes.
questions.hint: Consider events in prophase I and metaphase I.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of cell division produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent cell?
questions.hint: Think about growth and tissue repair.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for the division of the cytoplasm that follows nuclear division.
questions.hint: It happens after telophase.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: During which phase of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles of the cell?
questions.hint: Spindle microtubules shorten and pull the centromeres apart.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A micrograph shows a cell in which the chromosomes are lined up along the equator of the cell. Identify the stage of mitosis.
questions.hint: Picture the chromosomes attached to spindle fibres from both poles.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why do chromosomes condense by supercoiling during prophase?
options: So they can be moved and separated without tangling or breaking
So that DNA replication can take place
So that crossing over can occur in every cell
So that the nuclear membrane can re-form
questions.answer: So they can be moved and separated without tangling or breaking
questions.hint: Consider what happens to very long DNA molecules when they are pulled apart.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a root tip squash, 24 cells are in mitosis out of 150 cells counted. Calculate the mitotic index. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells counted.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in a human gamete?
questions.hint: Meiosis is a reduction division.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which of these statements correctly compares mitosis and meiosis?
options: Meiosis involves two divisions; mitosis involves one
Crossing over occurs in mitosis but not meiosis
questions.answer: Meiosis involves two divisions; mitosis involves one
questions.hint: Count the rounds of nuclear division in each process.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which stage of meiosis does crossing over between non-sister chromatids take place?
questions.hint: It happens when homologous chromosomes first pair up.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the name of the structure formed when two homologous chromosomes pair up during prophase I.
questions.hint: It contains four chromatids in total.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the name of the point where non-sister chromatids remain in contact after crossing over.
questions.hint: The plural form is often seen in micrographs of prophase I.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which stage of meiosis does random orientation of bivalents occur?
questions.hint: Homologous pairs line up at the equator in this stage.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: An organism has a diploid number of 6 (n = 3). Ignoring crossing over, how many different combinations of chromosomes can be produced in its gametes by random orientation?
questions.hint: Use the expression 2 to the power of n.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is a likely consequence of non-disjunction during meiosis?
options: Gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes
Gametes that are genetically identical to the parent
questions.answer: Gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes
questions.hint: Non-disjunction means chromosomes or chromatids fail to separate.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain how meiosis generates genetic variation in gametes.
questions.hint: Refer to events in prophase I and metaphase I.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Outline why a higher than normal mitotic index in a tissue sample may indicate the presence of a tumour.
questions.hint: Think about what uncontrolled cell division would do to the proportion of dividing cells.

bus-hl.topic: Changing work patterns and technology in HRM — HL: industrial and employee relations

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for a working arrangement in which employees can choose their start and finish times, usually around fixed core hours.
questions.hint: The word combines “flexible” and “time”.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which definition best describes the gig economy?
options: A labour market of short-term, task-based work, often arranged through digital platforms
A system where all employees work permanent full-time contracts
A government scheme to create public-sector jobs
An economy based mainly on the music industry
questions.answer: A labour market of short-term, task-based work, often arranged through digital platforms
questions.hint: Think of app-based delivery or ride services.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Outsourcing is best defined as:
options: Using an external organisation to carry out a function previously done in-house
Moving the head office to a cheaper area of the same city
Training employees to do several jobs
questions.answer: Using an external organisation to carry out a function previously done in-house
questions.hint: The work moves outside the business, not necessarily outside the country.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Offshoring is best defined as:
options: Relocating business activities to another country
Hiring temporary staff during busy periods
Allowing employees to work from home
questions.answer: Relocating business activities to another country
questions.hint: Think about national borders.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for bringing production or services back to a business’s home country after they had been moved overseas.
questions.hint: It is the reverse of offshoring.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a likely advantage to an employer of allowing remote work?
options: Lower office overheads such as rent and utilities
questions.answer: Lower office overheads such as rent and utilities
questions.hint: Consider the costs of running a building.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of the gig economy for workers?
options: Lack of job security and employment benefits
Automatic membership of a pension scheme
questions.answer: Lack of job security and employment benefits
questions.hint: Gig workers are often classed as self-employed.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a likely benefit to businesses of the immigration of skilled workers?
options: It helps to fill skills shortages
It always reduces the need for training
It removes the need for recruitment
It guarantees lower wage costs for all jobs
questions.answer: It helps to fill skills shortages
questions.hint: Think about the supply of labour with particular qualifications.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for the use of machines, robots or computer systems to perform tasks previously done by workers.
questions.hint: It is closely linked to the impact of technology on jobs.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Collective bargaining is best described as:
options: Negotiation between employee representatives and management over pay and working conditions for a group of workers
Each employee negotiating their own contract individually
A government setting the minimum wage
questions.answer: Negotiation between employee representatives and management over pay and working conditions for a group of workers
questions.hint: The key word is “collective”.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of the following is a form of industrial action short of a strike?
questions.hint: Employees continue working, but only do exactly what their contract requires.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of the following is a method that management might use during an industrial dispute?
questions.hint: Three of the options are actions taken by employees.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In which method of conflict resolution does an independent third party make a decision on the dispute, which both sides may agree in advance to accept?
questions.hint: In the other third-party method, the independent person only helps the two sides talk.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two disadvantages to a business of offshoring its customer service operations.
questions.hint: Consider quality, communication and reputation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Analyse one advantage and one disadvantage of flexitime for employees.
questions.hint: Think about work–life balance and teamwork.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Evaluate whether a strong trade union is beneficial to a business.
questions.hint: Consider communication with the workforce as well as labour costs and flexibility; reach a justified conclusion.

bus-sl.topic: Changing work patterns and technology in HRM

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which arrangement describes remote working?
options: Employees carry out their jobs away from the employer’s premises, often using digital technology
Employees share one full-time job between two people
Employees are moved to a different branch abroad
questions.answer: Employees carry out their jobs away from the employer’s premises, often using digital technology
questions.hint: Think about where the work takes place.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a flexitime system, what is the name for the fixed period of the day when all employees must be at work?
questions.hint: It is the “centre” of the working day.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: How are workers in the gig economy usually paid?
options: By the hour with guaranteed overtime
questions.hint: Each “gig” is a separate piece of work.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is the best example of a gig economy worker?
options: A freelance delivery rider who accepts jobs through an app
A civil servant with a fixed contract
questions.answer: A freelance delivery rider who accepts jobs through an app
questions.hint: Look for short-term, platform-based work.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A contract that does not guarantee the worker any minimum number of hours is called a ___ contract.
questions.hint: The guaranteed number of hours is nothing at all.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a common reason for a business to outsource a function such as payroll?
options: To access specialist expertise at a lower cost
To gain more direct control over quality
To increase the number of permanent employees
To avoid all contracts with other firms
questions.answer: To access specialist expertise at a lower cost
questions.hint: Think about what a specialist provider can offer.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a risk of outsourcing?
questions.hint: Someone else is now doing the work.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for moving business activities to another country.
questions.hint: The work goes “off the shore” of the home country.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a likely reason for a business to reshore production?
options: Rising labour costs and long supply chains overseas
Lower transport costs from distant factories
questions.answer: Rising labour costs and long supply chains overseas
questions.hint: Consider why offshoring may stop being attractive.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for the emigration of highly skilled and educated workers from a country.
questions.hint: It is a two-word expression about losing talent.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is a likely effect on a country’s businesses when many skilled workers emigrate?
options: Skills shortages in the home country
Lower recruitment costs for skilled jobs
An increase in the supply of skilled labour at home
questions.answer: Skills shortages in the home country
questions.hint: Think about the supply of labour left behind.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a benefit of remote working for employees?
options: Less time and money spent commuting
Clearer separation between home and work
questions.answer: Less time and money spent commuting
questions.hint: Think about the journey to work.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a possible negative impact of technology on employees?
options: Pressure to be available outside working hours
questions.answer: Pressure to be available outside working hours
questions.hint: Think about smartphones and work emails.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to a business of allowing employees to work remotely.
questions.hint: Consider costs, communication and motivation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two reasons why a medium-sized business might decide to outsource its IT support.
questions.hint: Think about cost, expertise and focus on core activities.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Discuss the impact of technology, such as automation and artificial intelligence, on employees.
questions.hint: Consider both job losses and new opportunities, then reach a conclusion.

chem-hl.topic: S2.3–S2.4 Metallic bonding and from models to materials

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which description best defines metallic bonding?
options: The electrostatic attraction between a lattice of cations and delocalised electrons
The sharing of a pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms
The attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer
questions.answer: The electrostatic attraction between a lattice of cations and delocalised electrons
questions.hint: Think about the “sea of electrons” model.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why are solid metals good electrical conductors?
options: Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice
The cations are free to move through the lattice
Metals contain ions that dissolve in water
Metal atoms share electrons in fixed pairs
questions.answer: Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice
questions.hint: In a solid, the positive ions stay in fixed positions.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why are metals malleable?
options: Layers of cations can slide over each other without the metallic bond breaking
Metal atoms are held by weak intermolecular forces
The electrons are fixed between pairs of atoms
questions.answer: Layers of cations can slide over each other without the metallic bond breaking
questions.hint: The delocalised electrons move with the layers.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which metal has the higher melting point, and why: sodium or magnesium?
options: Magnesium, because it has a higher ionic charge and more delocalised electrons
Sodium, because its atoms are larger
Sodium, because it has fewer delocalised electrons
Magnesium, because it forms covalent bonds
questions.answer: Magnesium, because it has a higher ionic charge and more delocalised electrons
questions.hint: Compare the charges of the ions each metal forms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why does the melting point of the group 1 metals decrease down the group?
options: The cations become larger, so the attraction to the delocalised electrons is weaker
The number of delocalised electrons per atom increases
questions.answer: The cations become larger, so the attraction to the delocalised electrons is weaker
questions.hint: Think about the distance between the nucleus and the electron sea.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the name for a mixture of a metal with one or more other elements, usually other metals.
questions.hint: Brass and bronze are examples.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why are alloys usually harder than the pure metals they contain?
options: Atoms of different sizes disrupt the regular layers, making it harder for them to slide
Alloys are held together by covalent bonds
The metal atoms in alloys are all the same size
questions.answer: Atoms of different sizes disrupt the regular layers, making it harder for them to slide
questions.hint: Think about what makes a pure metal malleable.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which two quantities are plotted on the axes of the bonding triangle (van Arkel–Ketelaar diagram)?
options: Average electronegativity and difference in electronegativity
Relative atomic mass and electron affinity
questions.answer: Average electronegativity and difference in electronegativity
questions.hint: Both axes use the same property of the elements.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Using electronegativity values of 0.9 for sodium and 3.2 for chlorine, calculate the difference in electronegativity for sodium chloride.
questions.hint: Subtract the smaller value from the larger one.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Using electronegativity values of 0.9 for sodium and 3.2 for chlorine, calculate the average electronegativity for sodium chloride. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Add the two values and divide by two.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A binary compound has a small difference in electronegativity and a high average electronegativity. Which type of bonding does the bonding triangle predict?
questions.hint: Metallic bonding is found where the average electronegativity is low.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which structural feature must a monomer have to undergo addition polymerisation?
questions.hint: The polymer forms when this bond opens up.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Name the addition polymer formed from ethene.
questions.hint: Add the prefix “poly” to the monomer name.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which is the repeating unit of poly(propene)?
questions.hint: Propene has a methyl group attached to one carbon of the double bond.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which electrons contribute to the delocalised electrons in transition metals such as iron?
options: Only the electrons in the inner shells
questions.hint: Transition metals have energetically close outer sub-levels.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why iron has a much higher melting point than potassium, even though both are period 4 metals.
questions.hint: Compare the number of delocalised electrons and the size and charge of the cations.

chem-sl.topic: S2.3–S2.4 Metallic bonding and from models to materials

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which statement best describes metallic bonding?
options: Electrostatic attraction between a lattice of cations and delocalised electrons
Sharing of electron pairs between atoms
Attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer
questions.answer: Electrostatic attraction between a lattice of cations and delocalised electrons
questions.hint: Think of a 'sea' of electrons.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the name given to the electrons in a metal that are not associated with any single atom.
questions.hint: They are free to move through the whole lattice.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why are metals malleable?
options: Layers of cations can slide over each other without breaking the metallic bond
The electrons are held in fixed positions
Metal atoms form strong covalent bonds in one direction only
questions.answer: Layers of cations can slide over each other without breaking the metallic bond
questions.hint: The bonding is non-directional.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which metal has the strongest metallic bonding?
questions.hint: Consider ionic charge and ionic radius.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why the melting point of the Group 1 metals decreases down the group. The main reason is that:
options: Ionic radius increases, so attraction between cations and delocalised electrons decreases
The number of delocalised electrons per atom increases
questions.answer: Ionic radius increases, so attraction between cations and delocalised electrons decreases
questions.hint: Each atom still gives one electron to the sea.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the term for a mixture of a metal with one or more other elements, usually other metals.
questions.hint: Steel and brass are examples.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why are alloys usually harder than the pure metal?
options: Different-sized atoms disrupt the regular layers so they cannot slide easily
The atoms in alloys are all the same size
questions.answer: Different-sized atoms disrupt the regular layers so they cannot slide easily
questions.hint: Picture the layers of a pure metal.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: On the bonding triangle, which two axes are used to place a binary compound?
options: Average electronegativity and difference in electronegativity
questions.answer: Average electronegativity and difference in electronegativity
questions.hint: The triangle is based on one property of atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A binary compound has a large electronegativity difference. In which region of the bonding triangle is it most likely to be found?
questions.hint: A large difference means electrons are transferred.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Two elements both have low electronegativity and a small electronegativity difference. Their compound is most likely:
questions.hint: Low electronegativity is typical of metals.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Element X has an electronegativity of 3.0 and element Y has 1.0. Calculate the average electronegativity used on the bonding triangle.
questions.hint: Add the values and divide by the number of elements.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which monomer can undergo addition polymerisation?
questions.hint: A C=C double bond is needed.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the name of the polymer formed from propene.
questions.hint: Add the prefix used for addition polymers.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What feature of the monomer is broken during addition polymerisation?
options: The pi bond of the C=C double bond
questions.answer: The pi bond of the C=C double bond
questions.hint: Only one of the two bonds in a double bond breaks.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why solid metals conduct electricity but solid ionic compounds do not.
questions.hint: Compare which charged particles are free to move in each solid.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Suggest why a material scientist might choose an alloy rather than a pure metal for a bicycle frame.
questions.hint: Think about strength, mass and corrosion.

comp-hl.topic: A1.3 Operating systems and control systems

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is a role of an operating system?
options: Managing memory allocation for running processes
Compiling source code into machine code
Increasing the clock speed of the CPU
questions.answer: Managing memory allocation for running processes
questions.hint: Think of what the OS controls between hardware and software.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the term for a signal sent to the processor to indicate that an event needs immediate attention.
questions.hint: A key press or a printer error can cause one.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does the processor do first when it receives an interrupt of higher priority than the current task?
options: Saves the contents of its registers so it can resume later
Ignores the interrupt until the task ends
questions.answer: Saves the contents of its registers so it can resume later
questions.hint: The current task must not be lost.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm gives each process a fixed time slice in turn?
questions.hint: Its name suggests going around a circle.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A disadvantage of first come first served scheduling is that:
options: A long process can make short processes wait a long time
Every process gets exactly the same time slice
It requires knowing the length of each job in advance
It cannot be implemented with a queue
questions.answer: A long process can make short processes wait a long time
questions.hint: Think about who arrives first.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which algorithm requires an estimate of how long each process will take?
questions.hint: The name refers to job length.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the name of the component in a control system that measures a physical quantity, such as temperature.
questions.hint: It provides input to the system.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the name of the component in a control system that produces movement or an action, such as opening a valve.
questions.hint: It turns signals into physical output.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a greenhouse control system, what is the role of feedback?
options: The output affects the next input so the system can keep conditions near a set value
It records the data for later printing
It removes the need for a processor
It allows the user to switch the system off
questions.answer: The output affects the next input so the system can keep conditions near a set value
questions.hint: Think about a heater turning on and off.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is an example of an embedded control system?
questions.hint: It is built into a device with one main job.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is meant by virtual memory?
options: Using part of secondary storage as an extension of RAM
Memory that is stored in the cloud
questions.answer: Using part of secondary storage as an extension of RAM
questions.hint: It is used when RAM is full.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In paging, memory is divided into:
options: Blocks the size of each function
questions.hint: Pages and frames are the same size.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement about segmentation is correct?
options: Segments are variable in size and match logical divisions of a program
Segments are always the same size as pages
Segmentation removes the need for memory management
questions.answer: Segments are variable in size and match logical divisions of a program
questions.hint: Compare with how paging divides memory.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of fragmentation can occur with paging?
questions.hint: The last page of a process may not be full.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain how an operating system makes it appear that several programs are running at the same time on a single-core processor.
questions.hint: Use the terms multitasking, time slice and context switch.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe how a thermostat-controlled heating system uses a sensor, a processor and an actuator.
questions.hint: Follow the data from the measurement to the action.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is an advantage of the round robin algorithm?
options: Every process receives processor time regularly
It never needs a context switch
questions.answer: Every process receives processor time regularly
questions.hint: Think about fairness.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which device is most likely to be used as a sensor in an automatic door?
questions.hint: The door needs to detect people.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What can happen if too much virtual memory is used?
options: Thrashing, where the system spends more time swapping than processing
The hard disk becomes RAM permanently
questions.answer: Thrashing, where the system spends more time swapping than processing
questions.hint: Secondary storage is much slower than RAM.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why interrupts are given different priorities.
questions.hint: Compare a power failure with a key press.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe how a thermostat-controlled heating system uses a sensor, a processor and an actuator.
questions.hint: Follow the data from the measurement to the action.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Market failure occurs when:
options: The free market fails to allocate resources to achieve allocative efficiency
The government sets a price ceiling
questions.answer: The free market fails to allocate resources to achieve allocative efficiency
questions.hint: Think of where MSB equals MSC.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the term for a cost imposed on a third party that is not reflected in the market price.
questions.hint: It is the opposite of a positive spillover.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does MSC stand for?
questions.hint: It includes private and external costs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: For a negative externality of production, which relationship is true?
questions.hint: The external cost is added to the private cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a negative production externality diagram, the free market output is:
options: Greater than the socially optimal output
Less than the socially optimal output
Equal to the socially optimal output
questions.answer: Greater than the socially optimal output
questions.hint: Producers ignore part of the cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is the best example of a negative externality of production?
options: A factory releasing pollutants into a river
questions.answer: A factory releasing pollutants into a river
questions.hint: Look for a third party harmed by output.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: For a negative externality of consumption, which relationship is true?
questions.hint: Consumption harms others, lowering benefit to society.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the term for a good that is overconsumed and harmful, such as tobacco.
questions.hint: It is the opposite of a merit good.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: On an externality diagram, the welfare loss triangle lies between:
options: The free market quantity and the socially optimal quantity
The origin and the free market quantity
The price axis and the supply curve
The demand curve and the price axis
questions.answer: The free market quantity and the socially optimal quantity
questions.hint: It shows the units where MSC exceeds MSB.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which government policy directly aims to make producers pay the external cost of pollution?
questions.hint: It shifts MPC towards MSC.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: At the free market output, MPC = $40 and the external cost per unit is $15. Calculate MSC in dollars.
questions.hint: MSC equals private cost plus external cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The free market output is 500 units and the socially optimal output is 380 units. Calculate the overproduction in units.
questions.hint: Subtract the optimum from the market output.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A welfare loss triangle has a base of 120 units and a height of $15. Calculate the welfare loss in dollars.
questions.hint: Use one half times base times height.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A limitation of a tax on alcohol to reduce consumption is that:
options: Demand is price inelastic, so quantity may fall only a little
It lowers government revenue to zero
questions.answer: Demand is price inelastic, so quantity may fall only a little
questions.hint: Think of habit-forming goods.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using a diagram, explain why the free market leads to overconsumption of tobacco.
questions.hint: Show MPB, MSB and MPC = MSC, then identify the welfare loss.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the use of tradable permits to reduce carbon emissions from firms.
questions.hint: Consider setting the cap, monitoring and incentives to innovate.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement defines a negative externality?
options: A cost imposed on a third party not involved in the transaction
A cost paid by the producer for raw materials
A tax paid by consumers on a good
A fall in price caused by excess supply
questions.answer: A cost imposed on a third party not involved in the transaction
questions.hint: Think about who bears the cost: buyers, sellers or someone else?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does the abbreviation MSC stand for?
questions.hint: It is the social version of MPC.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a negative production externality, how does MSC compare with MPC?
questions.hint: Society bears the private costs plus something extra.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A factory's marginal private cost is $40 per unit and each unit causes $15 of pollution damage to local residents. Calculate the marginal social cost per unit in dollars.
questions.hint: MSC = MPC + marginal external cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Compared with the socially optimal level, a free market with a negative production externality produces:
options: too much output at too low a price
too little output at too high a price
questions.answer: too much output at too low a price
questions.hint: Firms ignore part of the true cost when deciding how much to supply.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which term describes a good that is overconsumed because consumers underestimate its harm to themselves and others?
questions.hint: Tobacco and alcohol are classic examples.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In a negative consumption externality diagram, which relationship holds?
questions.hint: Consumption harms third parties, so the benefit to society is lower than to the consumer.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is the name of the triangle on an externality diagram that shows the loss of social surplus?
questions.hint: It represents lost welfare to society.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: On a negative production externality diagram, the welfare loss triangle has a base of 200 units (Qm − Qopt) and a height of $6. Calculate the welfare loss in dollars.
questions.hint: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Passive smoking is an example of which type of externality?
questions.hint: Who creates the harm here: a producer or a consumer?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which government policy directly aims to shift the MPC curve towards MSC?
options: A free advertising campaign for the product
questions.hint: The policy should make producers pay for the external cost.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why is information failure linked to the overconsumption of alcohol?
options: Consumers may not fully know the long-term health risks
questions.answer: Consumers may not fully know the long-term health risks
questions.hint: Think about what consumers know when they make their choice.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which market-based policy creates a limited number of pollution permits that firms can buy and sell?
questions.hint: The total amount of pollution is capped.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A tax on cigarettes is likely to be less effective at cutting consumption because demand for cigarettes is:
questions.hint: Smokers are often addicted, so how much do they respond to price?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain why a free market for electricity generated by coal leads to market failure.
questions.hint: Compare private and social costs and say what happens to output.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the use of a carbon tax to correct a negative production externality.
questions.hint: Consider effectiveness, measuring the external cost, elasticity and effects on firms and consumers.

en-hl.topic: The Handmaid's Tale: language, power and control

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The Handmaids' names are formed from 'Of' plus the Commander's first name. Which literary concept does this naming system best illustrate?
questions.hint: The name is built from a man's name.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Who in the Commander's household is NOT allowed to read?
questions.hint: Gilead restricts literacy for women in general.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word game, played in the Commander's study, gives Offred access to written words?
questions.hint: Letters on tiles.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does the scratched Latin message in the cupboard represent for Offred?
options: A link to another woman and a secret act of defiance
An official rule written by the Aunts
A prayer she must repeat daily
A password to leave the house
questions.answer: A link to another woman and a secret act of defiance
questions.hint: It was written by someone who came before her.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Gilead names its centres and shops with biblical phrases. What is the main effect of this?
options: It gives religious authority to the regime's control
It makes life feel more modern
It hides the shops from customers
questions.answer: It gives religious authority to the regime's control
questions.hint: Think about why a regime would borrow sacred language.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which term best describes Gilead's coined words such as 'Unwoman' and 'Econowife'?
questions.hint: They are newly created words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Complete the ritual reply: 'Blessed be the fruit.' — 'May the Lord ___.'
questions.hint: It refers to fertility.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Offred often revises her account ('It didn't happen that way'). What does this suggest about language and truth?
options: Language can never fully capture experience, and reconstruction is partial
She is lying to the Aunts
The Commander is editing her story
questions.answer: Language can never fully capture experience, and reconstruction is partial
questions.hint: Consider the reliability of any narrative.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Offred plays with words, e.g. reflecting on the many meanings of a single word. What does this habit reveal?
options: She keeps mental freedom through language
She is preparing to become an Aunt
She has lost interest in words
She wants to teach the Marthas
questions.answer: She keeps mental freedom through language
questions.hint: Thinking about meanings is an act the regime cannot see.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How does the 'Historical Notes' section reframe the issue of power?
options: It shows academics in the future controlling and even trivialising Offred's voice
It proves that Gilead never existed
It is written by Offred herself
It celebrates the Commanders as heroes
questions.answer: It shows academics in the future controlling and even trivialising Offred's voice
questions.hint: Who gets to interpret her story at the end?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which phrase best describes the effect of the Handmaids' red clothing and white wings on communication?
options: It limits vision and so restricts both seeing and being seen
It allows them to signal to each other
It makes them invisible to the Eyes
questions.answer: It limits vision and so restricts both seeing and being seen
questions.hint: Think about what the wings block.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What name is given to the regime's secret police, whose title suggests surveillance?
questions.hint: It is a body part linked to watching.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which global issue framing fits best for an Individual Oral on this novel?
options: The use of language by those in power to shape identity
The impact of tourism on coastal towns
questions.answer: The use of language by those in power to shape identity
questions.hint: Choose the one connected to the novel's themes.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Analyse how the novel presents the link between controlling language and controlling identity. Refer to at least two techniques.
questions.hint: Consider names, neologisms, ritual phrases and narration.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: To what extent is Offred's narration an act of resistance against Gilead's silencing of women?
questions.hint: Weigh her secret storytelling against her compliance and fear.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Evaluate how the 'Historical Notes' affect the reader's understanding of power and voice in the novel.
questions.hint: Think about who speaks last and how they treat Offred's account.

en-sl.topic: The Handmaid's Tale: language, power and control

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the novel, what does the narrator's name 'Offred' most likely suggest?
options: She belongs to a Commander called Fred
She is a member of the Aunts
She has chosen the name herself
It is her name from before Gilead
questions.answer: She belongs to a Commander called Fred
questions.hint: Split the name into two parts.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which group of women in Gilead is allowed to read and write?
questions.hint: This group trains the Handmaids.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What game does the Commander secretly play with Offred in his study?
questions.hint: It is a board game built on words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why is the Commander's word game a forbidden act in Gilead?
options: Women are banned from reading and writing
Games of chance are against the law
The board belongs to the Wife
It is only played by the Eyes
questions.answer: Women are banned from reading and writing
questions.hint: Think about what the game requires the players to do with letters.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Shops in Gilead are identified by pictures rather than written names. What does this mainly show?
options: The regime controls women's access to written language
Shops are trying to save money
questions.answer: The regime controls women's access to written language
questions.hint: Who would need pictures instead of words?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Complete the standard farewell used in Gilead: 'Under His ___.'
questions.hint: It suggests constant surveillance.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What effect do ritual greetings such as 'Blessed be the fruit' have on conversation between Handmaids?
options: They limit real communication and reinforce ideology
They show that Handmaids are free to speak
They are used only to mock the Commanders
questions.answer: They limit real communication and reinforce ideology
questions.hint: Can genuine thoughts be shared in a fixed script?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the term for a woman rejected by Gilead and sent to the Colonies?
questions.hint: The prefix 'un-' removes her identity as a woman.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which narrative feature lets Offred hold on to a private voice despite enforced silence?
questions.hint: Whose perspective do we hear the story through?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Offred remembers her real name but does not reveal it directly. What does keeping her name secret suggest?
options: She protects a part of her identity from Gilead
She has forgotten who she was
She wants to become a Wife
She is not allowed to speak at all
questions.answer: She protects a part of her identity from Gilead
questions.hint: Names in the novel are linked to identity.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The section at the end of the novel, set at an academic conference in the future, is called:
questions.hint: It presents the narrative as a historical document.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which Latin phrase, scratched inside the cupboard, becomes a private message of resistance for Offred? Write the first word.
questions.hint: It was left by the previous Handmaid.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which statement best links the novel to the global issue of power?
options: Control over language is used to control people's thoughts and identities
Wealth is shared equally among citizens
Power belongs to whoever has the best education
questions.answer: Control over language is used to control people's thoughts and identities
questions.hint: Think of who decides which words can be used.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain how the renaming of Handmaids helps Gilead to control them.
questions.hint: Consider ownership, identity and what is lost when a name is changed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How does Offred use storytelling as a form of resistance? Refer to the novel.
questions.hint: Think about why she keeps telling her story even if no one may hear it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Discuss how silence is presented in the novel as both a tool of control and a means of survival.
questions.hint: Consider when silence is forced and when Offred chooses it.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In which genre of Elizabethan-Jacobean drama does Othello belong?
questions.hint: The protagonist falls and dies at the end.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In the opening scene, Iago and Roderigo describe Othello with animal imagery to Brabantio. What is the purpose?
options: To provoke racial fear and disgust
questions.answer: To provoke racial fear and disgust
questions.hint: Who are they trying to anger, and how?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What rank does Iago hold, below Cassio's lieutenancy?
questions.hint: An older word for this rank is 'ancient'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Othello's speech to the Senate about how he wooed Desdemona with stories of his adventures mainly shows:
options: his eloquence and dignity, contradicting racist stereotypes
that he is ashamed of his past
questions.answer: his eloquence and dignity, contradicting racist stereotypes
questions.hint: Compare his language with what Brabantio said about him.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which statement best describes how Othello's language changes after Iago's manipulation in Act 3 onwards?
options: It becomes fragmented and full of crude imagery like Iago's
It becomes more poetic and calm
It switches entirely to prose comedy
questions.answer: It becomes fragmented and full of crude imagery like Iago's
questions.hint: Think about whose way of speaking he starts to copy.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Iago calls jealousy a monster that 'mocks / The meat it feeds on'. What does this metaphor suggest?
options: Jealousy destroys the person who feels it
questions.answer: Jealousy destroys the person who feels it
questions.hint: What happens to the 'meat' a monster eats?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which theme does Cassio's lament over losing his reputation most directly develop?
questions.hint: Reputation is how others see you.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Iago tells Othello that 'Good name in man and woman' is the 'immediate jewel' of their souls. Why is this ironic?
options: Iago himself is destroying good names
questions.answer: Iago himself is destroying good names
questions.hint: Compare what he says with what he does.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Emilia speaks out against Iago in the final scene. What does this achieve dramatically?
options: It reveals the truth and restores Desdemona's reputation
It shows Emilia's loyalty to Iago
questions.answer: It reveals the truth and restores Desdemona's reputation
questions.hint: What does the audience finally see happen?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In his final speech Othello asks to be remembered as one who 'loved not wisely but too well'. What concern does this show?
options: Concern for his reputation after death
Indifference to how he is remembered
questions.answer: Concern for his reputation after death
questions.hint: He is speaking about how his story will be told.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which critical approach would focus most on how the play constructs racial difference?
questions.hint: It examines power, empire and 'the other'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: For centuries Othello was usually played by white actors in dark make-up. How does this affect discussions of reception?
options: It shows how earlier productions shaped and distorted the representation of race
It proves the play is not about race
It means the play was rarely performed
It shows audiences disliked the play
questions.answer: It shows how earlier productions shaped and distorted the representation of race
questions.hint: Think about who was allowed to represent Othello on stage.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Iago's motives seem to shift and are never fully explained. What two-word phrase, often used by critics, describes this apparent lack of clear motive? (motiveless ___)
questions.hint: It means evil without clear reason.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Analyse how the play presents the relationship between race and Othello's vulnerability to jealousy.
questions.hint: Consider his outsider status, his self-image and Iago's techniques.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: To what extent is reputation more important than truth in the world of the play?
questions.hint: Use Cassio, Desdemona and Othello's final speech as evidence.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Compare how an early modern audience and a contemporary audience might respond to the presentation of Othello as 'the Moor'.
questions.hint: Think about attitudes to race, casting and performance history.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Othello is a general serving which city-state?
questions.hint: The play opens on its streets at night.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: To which island is the action moved in Act 2?
questions.hint: It is threatened by the Turkish fleet.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Why does Iago resent Othello at the start of the play?
options: Othello promoted Cassio to lieutenant instead of Iago
Othello insulted his wife in public
Othello sent him away from Venice
questions.answer: Othello promoted Cassio to lieutenant instead of Iago
questions.hint: Think about who got the job Iago wanted.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which object, Othello's first gift to Desdemona, becomes 'proof' of her supposed affair?
questions.hint: It is embroidered with strawberries.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Who picks up the lost handkerchief and gives it to Iago?
questions.hint: She is Iago's wife.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which character warns Othello against jealousy, calling it 'the green-eyed monster'?
questions.hint: The warning is ironic because of who is speaking.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Brabantio claims Othello must have used witchcraft to win Desdemona. What does this reveal?
options: Racial prejudice that cannot accept their marriage
questions.answer: Racial prejudice that cannot accept their marriage
questions.hint: Why can't he imagine she chose Othello freely?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Cassio repeats the word 'reputation' after he is dismissed. What does this show about Venetian society?
options: Public honour matters more than private character
Money is the only measure of success
questions.answer: Public honour matters more than private character
questions.hint: He has lost his rank because of one night.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which phrase does Iago say that reveals his deceptive nature?
options: I am not what I am
I am the Moor's true friend forever
questions.answer: I am not what I am
questions.hint: It is a reversal of a phrase meaning 'I exist'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Othello is often called 'the Moor' rather than by his name. What effect does this have?
options: It marks him as an outsider defined by race
It shows he is a king
questions.answer: It marks him as an outsider defined by race
questions.hint: How does labelling someone affect how they are seen?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which term best describes Iago's speeches alone on stage, in which he shares his plans with the audience?
questions.hint: The audience knows more than the other characters.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: The fact that the audience knows Iago is lying while Othello trusts 'honest Iago' creates:
questions.hint: The audience knows something a character does not.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How might a modern audience's reception of the play differ from that of its first audiences?
options: Modern audiences may focus more critically on the racism Othello faces
Modern audiences see Iago as the hero
There is no difference in reception
questions.answer: Modern audiences may focus more critically on the racism Othello faces
questions.hint: Think about changing attitudes to race over 400 years.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain how Iago uses Othello's sense of being an outsider to make him jealous.
questions.hint: Think about Othello's insecurity about Venetian manners and marriage.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How is reputation presented as fragile in the play? Refer to two characters.
questions.hint: Consider Cassio and Desdemona, or Othello himself.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Discuss whether Othello's tragedy is caused more by jealousy or by the racism of the society around him.
questions.hint: Weigh evidence for both causes before reaching a judgement.

fre-hl.topic: Paper 2 reading strategies — HL: No et moi, homelessness and invisibility

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Ce n'est pas la première fois qu'il oublie ses clés. » What can you infer?
options: He has forgotten his keys before
questions.answer: He has forgotten his keys before
questions.hint: « pas la première fois » means it has happened before.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In No et moi, what does the abbreviation SDF stand for? Write it in French.
questions.hint: It describes someone with no fixed home.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In No et moi, why does Lou first talk to No?
options: She is preparing a school presentation (exposé) about homeless women
questions.answer: She is preparing a school presentation (exposé) about homeless women
questions.hint: Think about Lou's school assignment.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In No et moi, where do Lou and No first meet?
questions.hint: Lou likes watching travellers arrive and leave.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In No et moi, how is Lou presented as a student?
options: Very gifted and younger than her classmates
Older than everyone in her class
questions.answer: Very gifted and younger than her classmates
questions.hint: She has skipped school years.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Les gens passent devant elle sans la regarder, comme si elle n'existait pas. » Which theme does this sentence best illustrate?
questions.hint: People walk past « sans la regarder ».

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Find the word in this sentence that means 'to pretend': « Elle fait semblant de dormir pour éviter les questions. » Write the two-word French expression.
questions.hint: Look at the words before « de dormir ».

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Il avait beau chercher, il ne trouvait pas de logement. » What does « avoir beau » express here?
options: Despite trying hard, he could not succeed
questions.answer: Despite trying hard, he could not succeed
questions.hint: The search continues but fails.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « La mairie a ouvert un centre d'accueil, mais les places sont insuffisantes face à la demande. » What is the writer's main point?
options: The new shelter is not big enough for the need
The town hall closed the shelter
There are too many empty places
questions.answer: The new shelter is not big enough for the need
questions.hint: « insuffisantes face à la demande ».

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In a Paper 2 text: « Contrairement aux idées reçues, la plupart des sans-abri ont déjà eu un emploi. » What is the purpose of « Contrairement aux idées reçues »?
questions.hint: « idées reçues » are assumptions people already hold.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In No et moi, Lou's friend Lucas is in her class. Is he older or younger than Lou? Answer with one word in English.
questions.hint: Remember that Lou is younger than her classmates.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « No ne parlait presque jamais de son passé ; ses silences en disaient long. » What can you infer about No?
options: Her past is painful and she avoids discussing it
She has a happy past she loves sharing
questions.answer: Her past is painful and she avoids discussing it
questions.hint: « ses silences en disaient long » — what do silences communicate?

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which word in this sentence shows the writer's critical tone? « On détourne les yeux, honteusement, devant la misère. »
questions.hint: Look for the adverb that carries a judgement.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Elle s'est enfin sentie chez elle. » Which French word shows that she had waited a long time for this feeling?
questions.hint: It means 'at last'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In English, explain how No et moi presents the invisibility of homeless people in society. Give one example from the novel.
questions.hint: Think about how passers-by react to No and how Lou sees her differently.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Analyse how the friendship between Lou and No challenges both characters. Answer in English.
questions.hint: Consider what each girl gains and what difficulties arise.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Chaque été, Léa passe ses vacances chez sa grand-mère en Bretagne. » What is the gist of the sentence?
options: Léa spends her summers at her grandmother's in Brittany
Léa lives in Brittany all year
Léa's grandmother visits her each summer
questions.answer: Léa spends her summers at her grandmother's in Brittany
questions.hint: Focus on « chaque été » and « chez ».

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Le musée est fermé le lundi. » On which day is the museum closed? Answer in English.
questions.hint: « lundi » is a day of the week.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Malgré la pluie, les élèves ont joué au football. » What does « malgré » mean here?
questions.hint: The pupils played even though it was raining.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Hugo a raté son bus, il est donc arrivé en retard. » Why did Hugo arrive late?
questions.hint: « raté » with « bus » is the key.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Find the French word in this sentence that means 'yet' or 'however': « Il fait froid ; pourtant, elle porte un tee-shirt. »
questions.hint: It introduces a contrast.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « La ville a décidé d'interdire les voitures au centre pour réduire la pollution. » What is the main purpose of the decision?
questions.hint: Look for « pour » + infinitive.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Je n'ai jamais vu la mer. » Which statement is TRUE?
options: The speaker has never seen the sea
The speaker sees the sea every day
The speaker lives by the sea
The speaker saw the sea once
questions.answer: The speaker has never seen the sea
questions.hint: « ne … jamais » is a negative.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Elle travaille comme infirmière à l'hôpital. » What is her job? Answer in English.
questions.hint: She works in a hospital caring for patients.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Les jeunes passent en moyenne trois heures par jour sur leur téléphone. » What does « en moyenne » mean?
questions.hint: It refers to a typical figure across many people.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Le billet coûte douze euros, mais les étudiants paient la moitié. » How many euros does a student pay?
questions.hint: « la moitié » means half.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Il a éclaté de rire en voyant le chien déguisé. » How did he react?
questions.hint: « rire » is linked to laughing.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Autrefois, ce village comptait mille habitants ; aujourd'hui, il n'en reste que deux cents. » What can you infer?
options: The village has always been small
questions.hint: Compare « autrefois » with « aujourd'hui ».

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In a Paper 2 text, a sentence states « Selon l'auteur, le bénévolat rend les jeunes plus confiants. » Which question type would this best answer?
options: What is the writer's opinion about volunteering?
questions.answer: What is the writer's opinion about volunteering?
questions.hint: « Selon l'auteur » introduces a view.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Nous habitons ici depuis cinq ans. » For how many years have they lived here? Write the number.
questions.hint: « depuis » + a period of time.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « Depuis qu'elle fait du sport, Inès dort mieux et se sent moins stressée. » In English, explain two benefits of sport for Inès.
questions.hint: Look at the two verbs after « et ».

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Read: « On dit souvent que les réseaux sociaux isolent les jeunes, mais ils permettent aussi de rester en contact avec des amis lointains. » In English, explain the writer's balanced view.
questions.hint: Find the idea before and after « mais ».

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What does the 'water–food–energy nexus' describe?
options: The interdependence of water, food and energy security
questions.answer: The interdependence of water, food and energy security
questions.hint: Nexus means connection.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which sector accounts for the largest share of global freshwater withdrawals (around 70%)?
questions.hint: Think about irrigation.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What term describes the water used to produce a good, which is 'traded' when the good is exported?
questions.hint: It is invisible in the final product.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which of these has the highest virtual water content per kilogram?
questions.hint: Animals need feed, which itself needs water.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Food security exists when:
options: all people at all times have access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
a country grows all of its own food
farmers export most of their crops
questions.answer: all people at all times have access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
questions.hint: The definition focuses on access for everyone.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why is desalination an example of the water–energy link?
options: It requires large amounts of energy to produce fresh water
It only works in cold climates
questions.answer: It requires large amounts of energy to produce fresh water
questions.hint: Removing salt from water needs power.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How can growing biofuel crops threaten food security?
options: Land and water used for fuel crops are not used for food
Biofuels reduce water use to zero
They lower energy prices for farmers only
questions.answer: Land and water used for fuel crops are not used for food
questions.hint: Think about competition for the same resources.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A country has 1.2 billion m³ of renewable water per year and a population of 2 million people. Calculate the water available per person in m³ per year.
questions.hint: Divide total water by population.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Using the Falkenmark indicator, a country with less than 1,000 m³ of water per person per year is said to face:
questions.hint: Below 1,700 is stress; below 1,000 is more severe.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which energy source most directly depends on river flow?
questions.hint: Dams turn moving water into electricity.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How does energy insecurity affect food production in many low-income regions?
options: Lack of affordable energy limits irrigation pumping, processing and storage
It increases the size of harvests
It has no effect on farming
questions.answer: Lack of affordable energy limits irrigation pumping, processing and storage
questions.hint: Which farming tasks need fuel or electricity?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Building a large dam on a river shared by several countries can lead to:
options: geopolitical tension over water allocation downstream
guaranteed food security for all countries
questions.answer: geopolitical tension over water allocation downstream
questions.hint: Who controls the flow after the dam is built?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Exporting water-intensive crops from a dry country to a wet country is an example of:
options: a net export of virtual water from a water-scarce region
questions.answer: a net export of virtual water from a water-scarce region
questions.hint: Follow the hidden water in the crops.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the term for removing groundwater faster than it is naturally replaced, often to irrigate crops?
questions.hint: It leads to falling water tables.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Analyse how climate change could intensify pressures within the water–food–energy nexus.
questions.hint: Consider droughts, rising energy demand for cooling and crop yields.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Evaluate the view that integrated management of the nexus is more effective than managing water, food and energy separately. Refer to a case study.
questions.hint: Weigh trade-offs, governance and stakeholders.

hist-hl.topic: Comparing Haiti and Kenya: independence and identity

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Before independence, Haiti was the French colony known as:
questions.hint: It occupied the western part of the island of Hispaniola.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did Haiti declare independence?
questions.hint: It was declared on 1 January, after the revolution that began in 1791.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year did Kenya gain independence from Britain?
questions.hint: It was in December, about a decade after the Emergency began.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What name is commonly given to the armed anti-colonial uprising in Kenya in the 1950s?
questions.hint: The British declared a State of Emergency in response.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What was a major cause of the Haitian Revolution?
options: The brutality of slavery on plantations
Opposition to a British trade tax
questions.answer: The brutality of slavery on plantations
questions.hint: Think about the majority of the colony's population.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which issue was central to the grievances of the Kikuyu in colonial Kenya?
options: Loss of land to European settlers
questions.answer: Loss of land to European settlers
questions.hint: The highlands were reserved for settlers.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Haiti's independence was significant because it was the first independent nation to emerge from:
options: a successful revolt of enslaved people
questions.answer: a successful revolt of enslaved people
questions.hint: Consider who led and fought the revolution.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: The name 'Haiti' was chosen after independence. Where does it come from?
options: The Indigenous Taíno name for the island
The name of a Spanish ship
questions.answer: The Indigenous Taíno name for the island
questions.hint: The new state rejected the colonial name.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which statement best compares the METHODS of independence in Haiti and Kenya?
options: Haiti won through a full revolutionary war; Kenya combined armed revolt with political negotiation
Both won only through peaceful negotiation
Kenya fought a long naval war; Haiti used elections
questions.answer: Haiti won through a full revolutionary war; Kenya combined armed revolt with political negotiation
questions.hint: Think about how the final transfer of power happened in each.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which Swahili slogan, meaning 'let us all pull together', was used to build national unity in independent Kenya?
questions.hint: It still appears on Kenya's coat of arms.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In 1825 France demanded what from Haiti in exchange for recognising its independence?
options: The return of all land to the Taíno
questions.hint: It burdened Haiti's economy for generations.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which challenge to national identity did Kenya face after independence?
options: Uniting many different ethnic groups within colonial borders
Choosing a new language for the Caribbean
questions.answer: Uniting many different ethnic groups within colonial borders
questions.hint: Colonial borders grouped many peoples together.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: For a comparative essay, which inquiry question works best for both cases?
options: To what extent did the methods used to gain independence shape national identity?
How many miles is Haiti from Kenya?
When was the first railway built in Haiti?
questions.answer: To what extent did the methods used to gain independence shape national identity?
questions.hint: It must allow comparison and argument.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Compare the causes of independence in Haiti and Kenya.
questions.hint: Consider slavery, land, economic exploitation and external influences.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: To what extent did the violence of the independence struggle shape identity-building in Haiti and Kenya?
questions.hint: Weigh similarities and differences, then reach a supported judgement.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Evaluate the role of international factors in the achievement of independence in both cases.
questions.hint: Think about the French Revolution and post-Second World War decolonisation.
